original_question: For n > 3, does there exist a smooth contractible hypersurface in C^n whose logarithmic Kodaira dimension is of general type?
target_in_paper: Nearest paper-faithful target: the Zaidenberg-style open problem in the contractible-hypersurface/exotic-affine-space part of arXiv:alg-geom/9506006, asking whether a smooth contractible affine hypersurface in higher-dimensional complex affine space can be of log-general type, i.e. have maximal logarithmic Kodaira dimension. The paper itself is a Montreal 1994 problem list rather than a theorem-numbered article. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9506006))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient complex affine space, the hypersurface condition, smoothness, topological contractibility, the restriction to dimensions greater than 3, and the intended birational-geometric property: log-general type/maximal logarithmic Kodaira dimension. This is exactly the right narrow corner of the paper's contractible-hypersurface discussion. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1993__217__251_0.pdf))
missing_details: Replace the ambiguous phrase "whose logarithmic Kodaira dimension is of general type" by the standard stand-alone formulation "which is of log-general type," equivalently "whose logarithmic Kodaira dimension satisfies \bar\kappa(X)=\dim X"; for a hypersurface X\subset \mathbb{C}^n this means \bar\kappa(X)=n-1. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1993__217__251_0.pdf))

State explicitly that X is an affine algebraic hypersurface over the field \mathbb{C}, i.e. a smooth closed codimension-1 subvariety X\subset \mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{C}}=\mathbb{C}^n. ([numdam.org](https://numdam.org/item/CIF_1993__S24__57_0.pdf))

Specify that "contractible" is meant topologically in the usual Euclidean/complex topology on X(\mathbb{C}); this is the convention used throughout the surrounding literature on exotic affine spaces. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1993__217__251_0.pdf))

Clarify the quantifier on n. As written, "For n>3" can be read either as "for every integer n\ge 4" or "for some n\ge 4"; a stand-alone research question should choose one. The draft most naturally reads as the former. ([numdam.org](https://numdam.org/item/CIF_1993__S24__57_0.pdf))

Make explicit that the problem is about hypersurfaces, not general contractible affine varieties. This matters because Zaidenberg's known log-general-type contractible examples arise first as surfaces, and products X\times \mathbb{C}^{n-2} give exotic affine structures but are not hypersurfaces; indeed they cannot even embed regularly as \mathbb{C}^{n-1} inside those product examples. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1993__217__251_0.pdf))
refined_question: For every integer n\ge 4, does there exist a smooth affine hypersurface X\subset \mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{C}}=\mathbb{C}^n such that X is contractible in the Euclidean topology and is of log-general type, i.e. its logarithmic Kodaira dimension is maximal: \bar\kappa(X)=\dim X=n-1? ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1993__217__251_0.pdf))
justification: alg-geom/9506006 is not a theorem/proposition paper with a Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; it is a conference problem list. So the right reconstruction has to come from the nearby contractible-variety/exotic-affine-space context rather than from nonexistent numbered results in that paper. The surrounding literature shows the exact tension your draft is trying to capture: Zaidenberg had already constructed countably many smooth contractible affine surfaces of hyperbolic/log-general type and used them to produce exotic affine structures on \mathbb{C}^n for n\ge 3, but those examples are products, not hypersurfaces, and in fact do not admit injective regular maps from \mathbb{C}^{n-1}. Kraft's survey, written at essentially the same moment, records that all smooth contractible surfaces of logarithmic Kodaira dimension 1 can be realized as hypersurfaces in \mathbb{A}^3, while infinitely many log-general-type contractible surfaces were also known. Kaliman-Makar-Limanov's C^4 hypersurface paper then makes clear that smooth contractible hypersurfaces in higher ambient dimension were being studied precisely in this period, and that some such hypersurfaces had only nonnegative logarithmic Kodaira dimension. Put together, the nearest sharp paper-faithful formulation is the higher-dimensional hypersurface existence question with maximal logarithmic Kodaira dimension, stated using \bar\kappa(X)=n-1 rather than the looser phrase in the draft. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9506006))
